RESOLVED: positional, and the position cannot be reached from both sides. A '[' reached from UsageDeclaration's FeatureSpecializationPart is a MultiplicityRange (SysML 8.2.2.6.6); a '[' reached after a primary expression operand is a BracketExpression (KerML 8.2.5.8.2). The hypothesis held for every corpus shape. The decisive line is `attribute mass : MassValue[1] = 1200 [kg];`, which writes BOTH roles and parses: multiplicity_part is reachable only from feature_specialization_part, which sits inside UsageDeclaration, and a UsageDeclaration is finished before the ValuePart's '=' is read, so the two can never contend for one token. What separates the productions themselves is the OPERAND: a BracketExpression has one before the '[' and a MultiplicityRange has none, which is what tests/rejection/bracket-expression-needs-an-operand.sysml holds. The corpus also writes a bracketed name (`[one]`, `[spatialCF]`, `[source]`) that is indistinguishable from a multiplicity bound by CONTENT, which is why content was never a candidate rule. Both roles are implemented and 297 corpus files are no longer blocked on this; acceptance went 32 to 39 .sysml when BracketExpression landed.

Is MAX_DEPTH = 400 in crates/sv2-syntax/src/parser.rs the right recursion limit, and should it be configurable? It was introduced because the recursive expression parser OVERFLOWED THE STACK, which aborts the process and so is strictly worse than the panic invariant 3 forbids. Measured thresholds before the guard: unary operators between 2000 and 5000 levels, parenthesised expressions and nested bodies between 5000 and 10000. 400 is far past anything a person writes, but it is a number nobody derived from a source, and it changes what the parser accepts.

WIDENED by the postfix expressions. DEPTH IS A PROPERTY OF THE TREE, NOT OF THE PARSER'S RECURSION, and the feature chain proved it: `postfix_tail` is a LOOP and uses no stack at all, yet a 50000-link chain aborted a test thread, because every link wraps the last and the tree is as deep as the chain is long. Folding also stopped being linear at that size. Chains and brackets are therefore counted against the same budget as nested bodies. Anything else that folds -- IndexExpression, FunctionOperationExpression, CollectExpression, SelectExpression, all of which join the same loop -- must count too, and the loop is the place to enforce it once.
